motion_commands.comment: MotionCommandID values accepted by the Meca500 in the MotionCommand field of the cyclic output assembly. Transcribed by hand from Table 8 of the programming manual, because no vendor definition file publishes them: neither the EDS, the GSDML nor the ESI. tools/eds_to_spec.py merges this table into the generated specification.

source.document: Meca500 programming manual, 4. Communicating over cyclic protocols, Table 8

notes: A command is sent by changing MotionControl_MoveId to a new non-zero value while MotionControl_Setpoint is set.

The velocity-mode commands listed under 'velocity_mode' work the other way round: they run continuously while MoveId is 0 and Setpoint is 1. Queueing one by changing MoveId instead fills the motion queue with a copy every cycle.
Identifiers 10000 to 19999 set the robot variable whose cyclic id matches the identifier.
Commands marked '†' in the manual take the same arguments, in the same order, as the TCP/IP command of the same name; extra arguments are ignored.

arguments.GripperAction: argument 1 is 0 to close the gripper, 1 to open it
arguments.ClearRobotHoming: clears the homing, forcing drive reinitialisation on the next activation

dynamic_data_types.comment: DynamicDataTypeID values accepted in DynamicTypeCfg0..3 of the output assembly. The robot echoes the type back in DynamicType0..3 and publishes up to six floats in the matching DynamicData slot. Transcribed by hand from Table 12 of the programming manual: no vendor definition file publishes them, exactly as with the motion command identifiers. tools/eds_to_spec.py and tools/update_dynamic_data_types.py merge this table into the specification.

source.document: Meca500 programming manual, 4.4.6 Dynamic data configuration, Table 12

notes: Type 0 is Automatic: the robot cycles through every available type, a different one each cycle, which is the easiest way to receive everything periodically.
Every type returns six values; the unused ones are zero.
Identifiers 10000 to 19999 report the robot variable whose cyclic id matches, which is how Get variable works.
No type exists for information already carried by a dedicated field, such as the target joint set or the target end-effector pose.

descriptions.Automatic: The robot chooses a type and changes it every cycle, going through all of them in a round-robin manner
descriptions.ActualEndEffectorPose: Measured pose x, y, z, alpha, beta, gamma
descriptions.ActualJointVelocity: Measured joint velocities, in degrees per second
descriptions.MotionQueueVelocities: joint velocity, joint acceleration, Cartesian linear velocity, Cartesian angular velocity, Cartesian acceleration, joint velocity limit, all in percent
